name: Shinab
title: King of Admah
summary: Shinab was the king of Admah, one of the five cities on the Jordan Plain. He was among the kings who rebelled against King Chedorlaomer of Elam after twelve years of subjugation and took part in the battle in the Valley of Siddim. He is mentioned in connection with Abraham's rescue mission for Lot.

keyEvents.title: Alliance against Chedorlaomer
keyEvents.description: Shinar was one of five kings on the Jordan Plain who had been subject to King Chedorlaomer for twelve years but rebelled in the thirteenth year.

keyEvents.title: The Battle in the Valley of Siddim
keyEvents.description: Shinar and the four allied kings fought against Chedorlaomer and his allies in the Valley of Siddim, which was full of tar pits. They were defeated and fled.

keyEvents.title: Defeat and Plundering
keyEvents.description: After their defeat, the enemies plundered Sodom and Gomorrah, taking all their goods and food supplies, including Lot, Abraham's nephew.

keyEvents.title: Abraham's Rescue Mission
keyEvents.description: Abraham gathered 318 men, pursued Chedorlaomer's forces, defeated them, and brought back all the goods, along with Lot and the other captives. This directly impacted Shinar's kingdom.

keyEvents.title: The Destruction of Admah
keyEvents.description: Admah, the city over which Shinar ruled, was later destroyed together with Sodom and Gomorrah because of the wickedness of its inhabitants. This event is mentioned as a warning in later biblical texts.
